messages:
maeve: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a reproducible mem growth on dedicated when continuous batching merges several long-context requests. Started after the kernel selector change last week.
ryan: ugh, can you paste the smallest repro + logs?
maeve: Yep — reproducible on cc-ded-06 with model=gptx-70b-16k, seqs ~12k. Flamegraph attached (shortlink): https://short.host/fg-4999. Key log snippet: 
```
kv_cache: slot_count=512 active=498 resident_bytes=12.1GB growth=+120MB/min
batcher: merged_batch_id=442 head_of_line_wait=230ms merge_reason=early_threshold
```
zhen: interesting — head_of_line_wait spikes when merged batch contains 1x short + 3x long requests?
maeve: yep. pattern: a longctx request lands, short requests queued behind, then an early-merge groups them -> short stalls on KV lookups waiting for long's KV page fetches, and the long keeps pinning new slots. Eventually fragmentation + slow reclaim => memory climbs.
olga: have you tried disabling early-merge or changing the merge gating?
maeve: tried toggling `runtime.enable_early_merge = false` — mem growth stops but p95 latency for short requests jumps ~60ms. So it's a tradeoff.
ryan: can you run a variant with `kv.eviction_interval=1s` and `kv.prefetch=false`? that should surface whether prefetch interacts badly with merged batches.
maeve: ran that — slight improvement to peak resident but still slow leak on long runs (10k+ tokens). logs: 
```
kv: eviction_scan=1s reclaimed=2.4MB/s
kv: prefetch=off merge_window=60ms
```
perf-bot: perf/regression detected: kernel-selector v2 -> +3% resident for longctx workloads (internal ticket RW-1173).
zhen: could be a KV fragmentation + slab allocation pattern when the merged batch interleaves slot lifetimes. We should check slab-buckets heatmap from heap profile.
maeve: attaching heap diff excerpt and a small repro script below. Repro uses concurrent curl clients (3 short, 1 long) repeatedly.
```bash
# repro loop
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.cc:443/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REPRO_KEY" -d '{"model":"gptx-70b-16k","inputs":[{"id":"long","text":"<'$(head -c 12000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'A')'>'"},{"id":"short1","text":"hi"},{"id":"short2","text":"status?"}],"batching":{"mode":"continuous","merge_window_ms":60}}' &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
olga: thanks — can you try `kv.merge.split_threshold=0.2` (i.e., split merged batches if long/short size ratio > 5) and retest?
maeve: doing that now on cc-ded-06. quick numbers after 15m: resident stabilized, head_of_line_wait decreased, but overall token throughput dropped ~4%.
ryan: tradeoffs okay for now if it fixes leak. We should instrument per-slot lifetime and increase the reclamation priority for slots owned by merged long requests.
zhen: agree. Also add a guarded fast-path in the batcher: avoid merging if estimated KV page miss rate for the resulting batch > X. We can use historical kernel hints to estimate.
maeve: filed a short ticket RW-1199 with reproducer + flamegraph + heap diff. Deploying a test with `kv.merge.split_threshold=0.2` and `kv.eviction_aggressiveness=high` for 2h window. Will report back. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: started deployment to cc-ded-06 with flags: runtime.enable_early_merge=false, kv.merge.split_threshold=0.2, kv.eviction_aggressiveness=high. rollout id dpl-8842.
maeve: preliminary: after 40m the steady-state resident is ~9.8GB (was 12.1GB) and p95 short latency increased +35ms vs default. Keeping this config for further analysis.
ryan: good. next items: (1) add per-slot lifetime metrics to Console, (2) add merge-gating heuristic based on predicted KV miss cost, (3) consider a kernel tweak to pre-allocate contiguous slab runs for longctx merges to reduce fragmentation.
olga: I'll pick up #1, zhen can prototyping #2, and ryan/maeve can spec #3.
maeve: thanks all — will update RW-1199 with timed metrics and a before/after flamegraph. If anyone wants to repro locally, ping me for the REPRO_KEY.
